researchQuestion: At each TL, what Reactor output and subsystem Tactical Power economy preserves meaningful tactical scarcity, multiple viable ship architectures, and useful degraded/emergency behavior without chronic starvation or effectively unlimited power?

operationalSupplySweep.note: Absolute supply curve, deliberately broader than the CP160-PF4 5-13 TP scaffold and broad enough to include/exceed historical CP110 high-TL candidates.

poweredAuxTpInterpretation: CP160-PF4 magnitudes/mechanics are held fixed. Shield Hardener, Energized Armor, Field Stabilizer, and Damage Control/Repair Drone TP operating costs remain provisional and are measured as resource-economy variables rather than retuned combat magnitudes.
repairDroneIntegrationBoundary: The whole-ship demand model includes a second distinct-target Damage Control TP request when a Damage Crisis presents multiple eligible targets. Full component-damage execution remains deferred because the current Python combat ecology still exposes hull-only Damage Control targets.
reactorDamageStateBoundary: Degraded and Emergency Reactor outputs are evaluated against the same exact/stochastic demand distributions as separate supply states. The current full-map Python combat ecology does not yet transition reactor component state during battle, so combat outcome sensitivity varies Operational output only.
allocationPolicy: Budget-aware deterministic priority allocation is evaluated per doctrine. Raw simultaneous demand is a stress diagnostic only; no requirement exists to fund every installed system every turn.
spacePolicy: One primary Reactor is the primary scarcity population; an optional second Reactor is evaluated as a legal architecture with explicit Space opportunity cost. Reactor Space 4-8 is a diagnostic sweep only and does not imply miniaturization promotion.
expectedStudyProducts: exact powered-architecture population and demand envelopes
stochastic doctrine demand distributions and allocation outcomes
same-TL full-map combat sensitivity across seven Reactor-output offsets, including mirrored one-Reactor versus two-Reactor architecture contests
evidence for a later selection/refinement checkpoint; no automatic PF5 promotion
